summary:
"Peter did not want to be at this party.
That was not unusual, exactly. He didn’t want to do a lot of things until he was already there, and then occasionally, it turned out ok. Sometimes his brain would do this thing where it treated being asked to participate in normal, high school social life like he was being asked to walk in traffic. Then, once he actually got somewhere, he would remember that people were not always terrible, music was sometimes ok, and sometimes there were snacks. Sometimes, he could even relax and have a good enough time.
This, however, was not one of those times."
~~~
After a party leaves Peter with memories he cannot name and a body he no longer feels safe inside, he begins to disappear in ways no one around him understands.
Tony knows something is wrong. May knows Peter is slipping. They can see the signs of an imminent collapse Peter refuses to explain. But Peter insists he’s fine, even as his demons pull him further under, threatening to drown him.
By the time Peter can admit what happened, the people who love him are not just trying to uncover the truth. They are trying to keep him alive long enough to survive it.

A Tony Stark experiment that promised to change the future spirals out of control when Peter Parker, as curious as ever, touches the teleportation prototype... and is pulled into a portal that drags him into another dimension.

Peter wakes up in Gotham, a city so dark that he can't help but feel afraid.

What is a nightmare for Tony could become Peter's chance to find the place where he truly belongs.

summary:
“My name is Peter Parker, you will not remember that fact in five minutes’ time, I am Spider-Man. It’s been two years since my identity has been erased from the world, two excruciatingly long years of being no one but the spider. I am a nuisance, a menace, and worst of all, emotionally damaged beyond repair. Maybe in the next life, not this one,” he raised the ball, making sure the camera saw it, “I managed to create a device, one that holds the smallest of fractions of the six infinity stones’ power. It will only be used on one person, and one person alone. Me.”
Peter looked up at the sky, the stars looking back at him. He closed his eyes, taking a deep breath before opening them back up and looking into the camera yet again. He gulped. He was ready. The pain he felt, the pain only he felt because of his powers, was reminded to him as he pressed the button.
There was no more Spider-Man, and the world sure as hell forgot his face and name, exactly five minutes after the broadcast was done. They only remembered how broken and sad the spider looked, and how he was now forever gone.

“Kid.”That pain in Peter's heart curled into a tight knot. His hardened eyes stared forward, softening slightly at the nickname.He looked away, his face contorting into something bitter and tired.
Tony paused, taking a long moment to really look at Peter.The last time he remembered seeing the kid was on a battlefield during the final fight with Thanos. Though he had been slightly injured, Peter had somehow still had that bright glow and smile to him, and that same light in his eyes.He didn't see that anymore.Sure, Peter physically looked around the same—though he had grown and matured some—there was something...different in his eyes.It was a look Tony recognized. summary:
At the end of dinner, they go to part at the door, and Peter gives Pepper and May a chance to have a private conversation to themselves by heading to the kitchen and starting up the washing and drying of the dishes that he and May normally do together on the rare night that they don’t eat directly out of take-out boxes.
Leaning against the doorjamb for just a moment, Pepper says, “Y’know, he reminds me of Tony a lot—though only the good bits, don’t worry. You have a really great kid on your hands, dear.”
Pepper leaves with a kiss at the door, the sort of kiss that tastes just a bit of new beginnings as it does of endings, of nebulae as much as supernovas, and May heads back to the kitchen, where she finds Peter helping wash the dishes.
May doesn't want to admit how her heart is in her mouth as she says, “So, what do you think, sweetheart?”
There is a reassurance on the tip of May’s tongue: I’m not trying to replace Ben. She’s never going to replace him, not really. But she makes me happy, and so do you, and— 
“I like her,” Peter says, “She makes you laugh.”
And something aches in May’s chest as she leans in and kisses his forehead, hiding the burning in her eyes.

Peter Parker is fifteen years old and has three identities to keep separate: a pupil at Midtown High, Spider-Man, and Tony Stark’s personal intern. Peter felt the hot Georgia sun beating down on his back as he hunched low, tucking himself between two rank garbage bins in the hopes they'd mask his scent. The haunting pleads for a quick death as she bled out on the ground in front of him.

For Jude Wells, everything was possible.
Not in a philosophical way, she meant literally. Airplanes? Easy. A dude building a suit of armor in a cave with scrap metal? Okay, impressive. A guy in a spider-suit swinging between buildings?
That was possible. Everything was.
Growing up in Queens, Jude developed two things: an insane ability to memorize specs, and a thing for people who wore masks. Not that she was a stalker. She just... noticed things. Nerds notice things. Nerds pick up on details. Nerds spend hours putting theories together when they should be paying attention in class.
And that's where the problem started.
Peter Parker sat two rows to her left. She could identify Cap's punches from Bucky's with her eyes closed, but she couldn't figure out why that guy annoyed her so much. It wasn't hate. Back in seventh grade, she'd had a tiny thing for him. The problem was, they'd never actually talked.

title: To Pick Your Poison
author: Office_Stapler
tags: adding tags as the story progresses
summary:
Death was permanent.
Never had he truly stood still at what would happen were death to come knocking on his door. Crimefighting had still been somewhat new to him. He had been fully aware of the danger that being Spider-Man brought forth. And yet, at merely sixteen years old, death creaked said door open.
He was drifting. How did he know he was drifting?
“Rarely do we grand favours.”
It sounded gentle. They sounded gentle.
“We do not wish to see you go so soon, little one.” It was like the voice—voices—came from multiple directions. He could not focus-
For a moment, he was cradled.
Until he felt the unforgiving feeling of a stone-cold wall nearly shattering his spine. Yet, finally, his mind went quiet.Or:Peter Parker managed to use the Infinity Stones instead of Tony Stark. In another universe, flowers bloom and rot simultaneously. Corpses roam the streets beside the living, trapped in their own minds, spirits unable to move on. Watches don’t tick. Children don’t grow up. Everything is perfectly, eerily still. Wars never break out, and Tony Stark is not dead. Well, not in the traditional sense. Nothing ever has to change.

Stephen Strange first realizes something is wrong when he starts seeing reflections of people who don’t exist in his mirrors. He becomes certain when he finds himself speaking with the dead. And then, as if things couldn’t get any worse, a broken Loki from another universe appears before him, begging for help.
Which would already be enough to deal with, except now a man claiming to be from something called the ‘TVA’ has arrived, insisting he’s Loki’s friend and that the fate of the multiverse rests in their hands. Peter Benjamin Stark was born on the 10th of August 2001 as a result of a one-night stand between billionaire playboy Tony Stark, and small-scale lab-worker Mary Parker. Tony Stark never expected or wanted himself to be a father, especially not after his past experiences with his own. Mary and Richard however, had always wanted a child of their own, it didn’t matter if he only shared DNA with one parent.
This meant that the boy went from Peter Stark to Peter Parker permanently, only hearing of his biological father through the news and short stories his mother would tell him, and the monthly cheque that his parents would receive in the mailbox. This divide between father and son continued even after Mary and Richard Parker sadly passed. Peter was barely 6 years old when he was transferred to living with his Aunt May and Uncle Ben, another couple cursed with Parker luck and the inability of having children of their own.
Even at 14 years old, Peter Parker had never met his biological father, and he was okay with that. If the man wanted nothing to do with Peter, then Peter wanted nothing to do with him. All Peter needed was his Aunt May, she was the only real family he had left.

In the race to acquire the Infinity Stones as quickly as possible - the only things that guarantee victory - both sides are desperate and willing to make sacrifices. As failures pile up, allowing Thanos to obtain five of the Stones, a desperate Tony uses a new prototype of a machine that has been steadily developed over the years to travel back in time and steal the Stones before they fall into the tyrant’s hands.
It is a shame that Tony did not account for one more factor that could determine the outcome of the battle - his sixteen-year-old son Peter, who, while following his dad stealing the Tesseract in 1970, accidentally altered the course of events, triggering a catastrophe whose consequences may be at least… weird.

summary:
Everyone who looks at Tony Stark only sees the mistakes, sees the reputation for bad decisions and how he nearly ran Stark Industries into the ground and nothing more than that. And while stakeholders speak with him at galas due to expectations and money and the like, there’s no reason why a random teenager off of the street is going to want to talk to the disgraced son of the illustrious Howard Stark, still a shining beacon enshrined in New York history.
And so Tony knows that the best course of action is to leave the kid to his studies and go back to his sad, lonely penthouse—
But then the kid opens his mouth and says, “Oh my god, you’re Tony Stark,” nothing but giddiness in his voice.
“Yeah, I am, kid,” Tony says, and even he’s surprised to hear that his voice has no edge to it. If anything, it’s amused. “And you are?”
“Peter Parker, sir,” the kid says, and for some reason, his cheeks are flushed, almost as if he’s…excited to meet Tony, and only a lifetime of media training stops Tony’s jaw from dropping clear off of his face and straight down to dig itself six feet under the tile flooring in here.
Because when was the last time that someone seemed genuinely excited to see him?

They, Peter and Tony, had been working in one of the labs together on a new type of web fluid that could conduct electricity. He had been working in a daze, mind still caught up in his Aunt’s death, of her bleeding out in his arms, when Peter accidentally dropped the beaker he was holding, reflexes too slow to catch it in time.

Glass shot out as the beaker clattered down, a shard of it nicking Tony’s ankle and letting the corrosive liquid splatter across his bare skin. “What the hell?! How could you drop that? We were so close to working that out, you’ve just destroyed weeks of work! Get out of my sight Spider-Man.”

Harley is everything Peter isn't: sharp-edged, defiant, openly hostile. The school was about to sell him to a brothel. Tony buys him instead, partly for Peter, partly because he can't stop himself from fixing things. Harley arrives terrified beneath his anger, convinced this is just another cage with nicer bars.
Now Tony has two omegas in his penthouse. One who's falling in love with him. One who can't even stand to be in the same room.In a world that defines omegas by submission and alphas by dominance, three people who don't fit anywhere else have to figure out how to fit together.

A snatch of an old prayer sings through Tony’s veins:
"I confess to almighty God, and to you, my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done, and in what I have failed to do—"
There is more to the prayer than that. More about the Virgin Mary and the saints and god. 
But the bit that always hit Tony, when he was a kid with a kneeler digging into his knees in between church pews, with the scars and bruises of his father’s fingers staining his skin, with a hope in his chest that was being torn apart by the pressures put on him by Howard Stark and Obadiah Stane and the board—
There are so many sins that have buried themselves between his ribs, actions taken by a man who had to suture together a heart of iron.
But it is not God that he needs to ask forgiveness from.
No—the only people that Tony needs to beg forgiveness from are the people that he hurt.
And top of the list is this boy, who he has somehow led to the conclusion that he would ever take his suit away again.

summary:
No one knew who Peter Parker was. No family, no friends, only a scholarship at a university and a dorm room; it was terrifying to be alone in the world, but it was also liberating. No one to hurt and no one to put in danger. Peter Parker was alone.
When his parents died, he had Ben and May; when Ben died, there was May; when May died, he had his friends. Peter, however, had no one. There was freedom in solitude, if no one knew him then no lie was being told.
Peter, however, needed a job, the college scholarship did not allow for some of the small luxuries that the friendly neighborhood guy needed.
That was when he met Nia, his classmate in an elective class who, unlike him, everyone noticed, though not in a complimentary way. She was the stereotype of the rocker girl who faced everything and everyone.
When he was paired in an academic project with Nia Bradford, Peter realized that maybe he liked her noise, the space she occupied, the imposed company. Getting to know Nia and being forced to face a past that cannot be forgotten, Peter realized that maybe being alone was not so liberating after all.
Being alone no longer seemed so appealing when Nia looked so beautiful with her pink hair.

A reimagining of BERO Brewing’s Dinner Dates Sounds playlist as a possible Spider-Man: Brand New Day arc, using songs, lyrics and details from the trailer to shape the narrative. More story outline than a proper fic (for the moment), the playlist drives the emotional beats, with lyrics used as framing and dialogue where it fits.

summary:
Peter Parker is nineteen and still hasn’t presented. It’s uncommon, but not unheard of—at least that’s what everyone tells him. Still, something about him has always felt off to alphas and omegas alike, like his body is waiting for something it hasn’t quite become yet. Peter tries not to care. He really does. But between Flash’s relentless comments and the constant pressure of a world that sorts everyone into neat, unequal categories, it gets harder to ignore.
Omegas are the most restricted of all presentations. Alphas are feared, envied, and too often excused for their behavior. Betas are considered “normal,” safe.
He’s exhausted in ways he can’t explain. Alphas make him sick. His body feels wrong in ways he doesn’t understand yet—and the closer he gets to certain people, the worse it becomes. Especially around Tony Stark. Especially around Oscar, Aunt May’s unsettling new partner who seems a little too interested in Peter’s “condition.”
Then come the headaches. The heat. The collapse. And when Peter finally wakes up in the Stark medbay, everything he’s been avoiding becomes impossible to deny: He’s presenting. And nothing about it is going to be simple.

After the spell, Peter Parker was alone.No friends, no family, no home to return to. New York moved on… but he didn’t.
Peter always knew luck wasn’t on his side—death, loss, sacrifice—like the universe itself was determined to remind him what it means to be Spider-Man. But when a mistake during a fight with a dimensional villain tears open an unstable portal, Peter falls into a world he doesn’t recognize: Gotham.
A dark place. Cruel. Perfect for someone like him.Or so he thinks.
Because, inexplicably, everything is different here. His wounds heal a little faster. The hits hurt a little less. Tragedy doesn’t find him quite as easily. As if someone—or something—were tipping the scales in his favor.
The problem is, Gotham already has vigilantes.And the Batfamily won’t ignore a teenager with impossible abilities, a grief he tries to bury, and a kind of luck that shouldn’t exist in their city.
Peter Parker only wanted to disappear.Fate—and magic—have other plans.

He could tell that Scott also felt helpless in this situation, However much power that the True Alpha held, it seemed useless here. Stiles honestly didn’t think that their lives could get any worse, especially considering how their PSATs went, yet the universe seemed to take that as a challenge.
“You guys just teleported here out of nowhere?” The man with the hearing aids asked, raising an eyebrow. “Honestly, not the craziest thing I’ve heard.”

summary:
Peter Parker didn’t mean to hack into Tony Stark’s private files. It just kind of… happened. But when Tony finds out, he’s not impressed, and Peter’s certainly not in the mood to deal with him. Too tired, too worn down, and way too done with trying to impress anyone. After all, what’s the point when no one ever sees you?
Peter’s double life as Spider-Man is wearing him thin, and he’s getting good at hiding behind sarcasm, snark, and a whole lot of attitude. But when Tony’s sharp eye cuts through the façade, he starts to see what Peter’s been hiding: a kid who’s been pretending everything’s fine, while the weight of his secrets, fears, and burnout crushes him.
What starts as a hostile meeting turns into something more complicated as Tony and Peter reluctantly begin to understand each other. But as Peter’s walls get higher, the pressure keeps building, and Tony finds himself drawn into the mess of Peter’s life, trying to pull him back from the edge. Peter, however, doesn’t know how to let anyone care... or how to ask for help.
In this story of mental health, growth, and found family, Peter and Tony both have to face their own scars, learning that sometimes, even a hero needs someone to catch them.

"The wind whipped through Peter Parker's hair as if the chocolate dipped curls had committed a personal offence against the violent gusts. Peter blinked against it, the sudden feeling of air blasting into his eyes drying them to such an extent that he wished that he had eye drops or his mask on. Peter forces a smile, but he can still hear it:
‘No, no, no, please, not him, not him, c’mon—’
He looks at Bucky and is instantly hit with the old Bucky face. Full block, expressionless wilderness, a six-lane blacktop of good luck guessing what’s going on back here. Miles of unreadable. The expression Bucky rocked for at least a year, when Peter was shiny and new to this, before all the smirks and smiles crept in, and before he was allowed to guess out loud what was behind them.
“You got to me fast,” Peter says, echoing Tony’s words, tone a touch flat. Trying to make it fact, not feeling, seems to be working. If Peter was to make this feeling, he doesn’t think he could deal. At all. Fact is safe. Fact is extremely not a feeling.
Bucky gives him a clipped nod.

Nothing.

Peter Parker is a ghost in his own story...
 
Months after the spell that erased him from everyone’s memory, he’s living in the shadows; no ID, no support, no one left to save. He works three under-the-table jobs, patrols at night in a suit held together by desperation, and survives on barely edible food and sheer willpower. His healing factor is failing. His body is crashing. And he’s not sure how much longer he can keep going.
Then he runs into Bucky Barnes. THE Winter Soldier.
Peter slips. Says too much. Moves too fast. And Bucky, who shouldn’t remember him, starts asking questions. Questions that could unravel everything.
Now Peter’s spiraling, terrified that one moment of recognition could collapse the universe all over again. With nowhere left to turn, he makes a choice: break into Avengers Tower, patch up his suit, and maybe, just maybe, survive one more night.
Before he collapses. For good.

"If something happens where the kid loses everyone, I want him to have someone."
"This is about you growing, kid, not me saving you."
"Hey, маленький паук, it's me? Your girlfriend's favourite hero. You'd sit on the other side of the couch during movie night, you didn't want to get too close because you thought I'd steal her away."
Everyone's gone. Not just Tony, Nat, and May - but everyone. MJ. Ned. And just when things were gonna be ok, the world decided it hates me. What Mr Stark would say if he saw me now?
"Hey... kid. We miss you here. Natasha says hi - she dyed her hair again. I told her red looks better on her. She keeps writing letters to Steve even though she never sends them. Says it's a long-distance relationship problem. I send them anyway. Vision misses Wanda every day. I think I saw him cry last week. If you see Steve... tell him I'm glad he finally got his dance. I guess that means I forgive him. Point Break, Legolas, the big guy, the little witch tell them hi."
I don't know what this place is. I don't know why I can hear them. I only know that the world forgetting you doesn't mean you stop existing and sometimes the dead remember you better than the living ever could.

summary:
Peter often wondered about the atomic bomb.
More than most teenagers should, probably. Though most teenagers weren’t vigilantes either. In any event, his wonderings had nothing to do with his extracurriculars. It was only tangentially related, in the way he seemed to be able to detonate his entire life in seconds, in an exorbitantly bright and colorful manner.
The thing was, an atomic bomb didn’t start with the explosion, although everyone always focused on that bit. Humans always did have a fascination with things that killed them, and from a humanitarian perspective, the damage was what was important. But coming from a more chemical perspective, the explosion was almost incidental.
The real danger was in the preparation, in the way two things that were stable on their own could be forced together under exactly the right — or wrong — conditions. Not inherently volatile, nor doomed from the start, but close enough and aligned until a reaction became inevitable.–-

summary: Spider-Man's eyes start to sting.He's supposed to wear bright spandex like skin and have white lenses for eyes. The brown hair sprouting from his head doesn't instill a sense of rightness in his heart. The slope of his nose and set of his lips might as well have been freshly molded out of clay. His eyes—a deep brown, framed by thick eyelashes—aren't something he's grown up seeing in the mirror every morning. He has to notice these things. They're not things he knows.There's no itch in the back of his head telling him that this is right. That this is him. It's just silent, and it makes something in his chest curl with a bone-deep dread.Who is he supposed to be?When Doctor Strange casts the spell to make everyone forget Peter Parker, it affects everyone—including Peter. With his memory of his civilian life gone, Spider-Man has to navigate a city he's pretty sure he's not supposed to be in with no real idea of his circumstances. Tony thought he knew everything about Peter Parker.

summary:
He came back alive. But he didn’t come back whole.
Peter Parker was missing for months. When the Avengers finally found him, he wasn’t the same. Silent, twitchy, and disturbingly obedient, Peter is a shell of the kid he used to be—rewired by Hydra, his memories shattered, his instincts weaponized.
Now, housed in the Stark lab, Peter doesn’t speak. He doesn’t recognize his friends. He doesn’t even know his own name. His body heals at terrifying speed, but his mind remains trapped in a haze of trauma, violence, and forgotten identity.
Tony Stark is determined to fix him. He doesn’t care how long it takes or how much it breaks him in the process. But as Peter’s behavior grows more animal than human—and the threat of what Hydra left buried inside him begins to surface—the line between saving the kid and losing him completely starts to blur.
Because Peter didn’t come back alone.

The first time Peter saw Cassandra, he recognized something familiar in her. It wasn’t her posture—though she was rigid, muscles tense like an animal ready to fight. It wasn’t her gaze—though there was an intensity in her eyes that spoke more of instinct and survival than of thoughts formed into words. It was something deeper. An echo of something he himself had felt for so long that he had almost stopped noticing it.
It was the feeling of being out of place in a world that wasn’t made for them.
Peter didn’t have many memories of his childhood before Gotham. There were fragments of images, shadows of voices he couldn’t name. He remembered hunger, cold, fear. He remembered running, fighting, learning that being faster and stronger meant surviving one more day. He remembered it in a visceral way, the same way Cassandra did. She didn’t quite fit into the Batfamily either. Not because they didn’t love her, but because there were parts of her they simply couldn’t understand.

This story begins with a threat that Peter Parker cannot ignore, despite his attempts to do so. Words on a screen turn into blood in the hallways of his school, and suddenly the life he’s built inside the Stark Tower feels like a target painted on everyone he loves. At the ripe age of fifteen, he has to make a choice no kid should ever have to make; burn the bridges behind him so his family stays safe. Tony was on the couch, an arm draped lazily around Pepper, both of them half-curled under a blanket. The hum of the movie filled the quiet, peaceful and ordinary—something Peter almost didn’t want to shatter.
Peter hadn’t meant to make a sound. He’d meant to sneak in quietly, just find Tony, maybe get patched up, maybe just… breathe for a second. summary:
Hazel Stark stood there, wrapped up like she’d walked straight out of a snowstorm — which, to be fair, she probably had. Her coat was huge, puffed up and dusted with tiny bits of melting snow. Her scarf was wrapped three times around her neck, her hands covered in thick gloves, and her boots were heavy enough to probably survive a blizzard.
She looked a little flushed from the cold, a few strands of hair peeking out from under her earmuffs. And when her eyes landed on him — sitting there pale, sniffly, and looking like death itself — her whole face softened.
“Oh, Pete…” she sighed, voice full of that gentle concern he loved and hated all at once.
Her hand came to rest on his back, rubbing slow, soothing circles as he coughed again. “I didn’t know it was this bad,” she murmured.
Peter managed a small, tired grin. “Y-you didn’t sound this worried in text,” he rasped out, voice barely there.

Peter raised an eyebrow. “Sick, huh? Well, that’s no fun. I can swing by and make sure you’re okay. Mr. Stark’s meetings won’t mind me missing one day.”

Love and fear are two sides of the same thread—and when Spider-Man nearly loses the person he loves most, that thread begins to unravel.
After a villain’s attack forces Peter Parker to confront his worst nightmare, he returns home shaken, haunted by a vision of watching you die. What begins as one night of tears and comfort slowly bleeds into something deeper—a fear that follows him into every corner of his life. Dr. Stephen Strange had begun to notice he was forgetting things.
It began with a vague sense of absence, that unsettling feeling you experience when you enter a room and forget why you went there in the first place. He had dismissed it as fatigue, nothing more than working too much and not getting enough sleep. 
But then he started to notice more… anomalies. 
It started with a gap, a two-week blank in his memory. It was recent enough that he couldn’t blame it on the natural fade of memory that comes with time. It was just…gone. Two weeks erased, as if someone had hacked it out of his mind. 
He was content to leave it alone until he stumbled across a note tucked into one of his books.
He did not recall writing the note, but he could identify his own unsteady scrawl. 
It was dated on the same day as the start of the gap in his memory. It had a series of numbers and a single warning: 
If you don’t remember this, be careful. DO NOT TRUST STARK.

the incredible burden of being a hero
summary:
With Uncle Ben, it was the same thing. That awful thought he’d tried to swallow all his life finally came true: one bad decision, one flash of selfishness, and he’d proven himself right. Love something and you’ll lose it. Care too much and you’ll ruin it.
That lesson carved itself into him, deep and permanent, like a scar that refused to fade no matter how much he grew around it. He spent years trying to make up for it—saving strangers, stopping crimes, answering police scanners at two in the morning—because maybe if he saved enough people, the universe would balance the equation. Maybe if he kept moving, he wouldn’t have to sit still long enough to feel the guilt gnawing at him.
But it didn’t work. It never worked. No matter how many times he patched the city back together, his own life kept splintering apart.

title: lost from home
author: solarreis
tags: Bruce Wayne Tries to Be a Good Parent
Other Additional Tags to Be Added
summary:
Reforming yourself from dust was not something Peter Parker thought would be so painful.
Well, saying that out loud now made him realize that, yeah, it would be excruciating.
Peter took a moment to try and orient himself once he felt his body completely form itself once more - which was still weird as hell - and took an uneasy survey of his surroundings. He found himself amongst a dimly lit alleyway that made the hair on his neck stand straight up. His shoulders tensed, everything in his body screaming at him that this was wrong.
This alley was not your typical New York City one, it warned him. His whole body tensed, muscles protesting and yet unable to back down. Peter willed himself to step forward, inching towards the mouth of the alley that provided little light. He tried not to think about the smell of blood and gunpowder in the surrounding area, nor the utter feeling of despair that covered him wherever he was like an oversized blanket.
First, he had to figure out where he was. Next, he had to find Tony.

Peter was tired. Tired of school, his internship, people, talking, everything. Every little action he had to do felt like a chore, like he was a kid having to wash the gross dishes for some pocket money but without the reward. Everyday without fail he woke up tired, he skipped breakfast, sat through boring class after class, tried to fake normality to his only two friends, ate barely enough dinner to not die of malnutrition in the freezing winter, went on patrol and attempted to sleep till the early hours of the morning. It felt as if he was watching his life from outside his body, like his soul was floating outside him and he had to painfully watch his lifeless body preform the exact same routine almost everyday without fail; the only variation being his occasional nights he'd stay at the compound or do his internship every Thursday. He felt his life go on and on in this endless loop that he couldn't seem to shake no matter how much he watched it repeat.

Peter’s breath came short, quick, and uneven.
He’d been closer before, hadn’t he? Closer to dying? He’d taken hits that should’ve flattened him. So why did this near miss make him feel like his soul was trying to crawl out of him?
His pulse was a drumbeat in his throat. He could still see the flash of the bullet in his peripheral vision, the narrow line it carved through the air, the way it had missed him. Barely, barely.
Spider-Man didn’t panic, but Peter Parker did.

The brilliant Spider-Man is back in business! Or sorta, for the matter. Peter Parker remains unknown to everyone. Sure, he made new friends, got a day job and was surviving, but he hasn't made himself much known yet. He didn’t make Peter Parker known yet—not enough for the matter.

tags: Tony Stark Acting as Peter Parker's Parental Figure
summary:
(Despite the tags, there is some fluff in this, in the form of flashbacks, so there's some slight comfort ❤️‍🩹)
 
Rhodey crouches down, bowing his head as he and Tony sit in silence, surrounded by New Yorkers who watch on with solemnity. None of them know who Peter Parker was, but they all know he was one of them. Peter Parker was just a kid. A kid who saved a little girl's life only ten minutes ago.
And now, the people of New York stand around him, mourning a young boy who died saving a life.
But Tony is the one who has to hold his child, knowing that he’ll never be able to hear Peter’s laugh again. He’ll never be able to hold him again. He’ll never be able to kiss him goodnight, or cuddle with him, or praise his work in the lab.
Tony is the one who has to hold Peter Parker, his child’s blood staining the streets of Queens.

Peter has no idea.
Sometimes Tony slips into his room in the middle of the night, at hours no one should be awake. Quiet and casual. As if it means nothing.
He sits on the edge of the bed like a shadow, like a secret he can’t admit even to himself.
Tony doesn’t know why he does it either. Only that it feels lighter here, like the world loosens its grip when Peter’s near.
But one night, Peter wakes. Half-asleep, half-dreaming. His head heavy, his thoughts still tangled in dreams. He blinks through the haze. Is it real? Or just another dream?
And there he is. Tony. Too close. Too real. Just like always. Just like every night in his head.

He wants. He aches. He just knows he wants him close.
Wanting. Needing. As if the dream never ended.

He turned in the tight grasp and looked down to be met with the sight of a little girl, no older than six.Peter held his arms out awkwardly, not quite sure what to do. He didn’t have much hands-on experience with children past a brief autograph, greeting, or picture. Now, there was a little girl hugging him, calling him her dad.Parker Luck at its finest, because nothing like this would ever happen to anyone except Peter.“Oh, uh…hi?” Peter squeaked out. He patted the girl’s head and squatted down so he could get to her level – it was hard to talk to people so much shorter than him. Was he even doing this right? He hadn’t made her cry yet, so that was a start.“Do you need help finding your dad?” he asked her softly.It’d definitely make more sense. Maybe she didn’t know where her dad was, saw Spider-Man, and figured he could help.The girl only looked at him, her big brown eyes melting a part of Peter’s soul. The city changes in slow motion.
  
  
    He learns its alleys. Its fire escapes. Its shadows.
  
  
    It’s not Queens. But it doesn’t try to be.
  
  
    And that, he realizes one night while watching the moon rise over Crime Alley, is its kindness.
  
  
    Gotham doesn’t ask you to be okay.It doesn’t pretend to save you.It just gives you a place to fall apart.
  
  
    And the people—They’re sharper here. Scarred. Softer than they look.
  
  
    Tim lends him books he doesn’t finish.Damian insults his hair, then teaches him how to hold a katana.Dick teaches him how to fall without injury.Cass teaches him how to move without being seen.Jason teaches him how to aim—and how to miss on purpose.

May Parker liked to think she’d seen it all—alien invasions, New York rent and enough broken bones to land her a guest spot on Grey’s Anatomy. But nothing could prepare her for watching her sweet awkward nephew crawling through the window at 2 AM… bleeding in spandex.
Between bandages, guilt, lasagna fueled threats, and a showdown with Tony Stark over some shady Italian restaurant to proves that maternal wrath is deadlier than any villain.

Pepper and Tony Stark’s biological kids, Morgan, Peter, and Harley, were kidnapped eight years ago. While Harley and Morgan made it home, Peter was lost all that time, believing his parents had abandoned him on purpose. When they finally find him, he’s scared, malnourished, and struggles to understand what it means to be part of a real family.
And then there’s Spider-Man. Peter’s doing everything he can to keep his identity a secret, but how long can that last? Will they still let him go out if they uncover his secret? Will he ever figure out how to fit into a family that genuinely cares about him? Reuniting is one thing, but rebuilding what was lost? That’s something none of them are prepared for. Keeping his double life hidden was hard enough before, now, with a family that’s protective and watching his every move, it feels impossible.

Blinding, burning green, sloshing around him like a heartbeat. Every inch of him felt like it was on fire.He didn’t know which way was up.His arms moved. Legs kicked. Not water. Not blood.The floor was metal. Cold. And beneath that, there were voices.The world tilted.Pain bloomed sharply behind his eyes, and then he rememberedHe died--Spider-Man is dead.At least, Peter was until he woke up in a Lazarus Pit with no memory of how he got there, no legal identity, and his sister Clara dragging him through back alleys in a city they don't recognize.Gotham is cold and unfamiliar. summary:
“So… I should probably tell you something,” the kid mumbled.
Tony frowned. “You didn’t get bitten by something again, did you? Is this gonna be like… Spider-Teenage-Ninja-Turtle or something?”
“No, no, nothing like that.”
Spider-Man slowly lifted his hand to his mask, fingers fumbling with the half-melted seals. Tony reached to stop him. “Hey, whoa, no pressure—”
But the mask came away with a soft tear, peeling off like a second skin.
And suddenly, everything went still.
The boy who looked up at them wasn’t a college intern. He wasn’t a grad student or a twenty-year-old prodigy.
He was a child.
Bruised cheek, split lip, a smudge of soot over one brow. His hair clung to his forehead with sweat and blood. His eyes- big, brown, and impossibly young- blinked up at Tony.
“Hi,” he said weakly. “I’m Peter. Peter Parker. I’m, uh… fifteen.”

Oh.

A plane coming in to land. The roof of the house a few minutes away. The Bang Tech Tower shining in the distance.Four things you can feel: the fabric and metal of the suit, clinging to the body. The vibration of the ventilation systems. The roughness of the lips. The coolness of a spring evening.Three things you can hear: breaking glass somewhere below. The hum of cars. A cat meowing somewhere in the alley.Two things you can smell: polluted city air. Tteokbokki from a stall a block away.One thing you can taste: Cherry lip balm stolen from Minho.Spider-Man exhaled, smiled, turned around and shot a web, flying down the floors.—Jisung knows how to deal with anxiety. Felix taught him how to ground himself long ago, before he was wearing a red and blue suit or had the weight of Seoul on his shoulders.But dealing with love? Condemnation? Trauma? Emilia Rogers–Stark was raised to be extraordinary.
She just wasn’t taught how to survive the weight of it.
Daughter of legends. Heir to impossible expectations. Brilliant, disciplined, and quietly relentless, Emilia has spent her life chasing perfection—building, creating, and controlling every fracture in her world before anyone else can see it.
Until the invention that was meant to define her begins to fail.
As pressure tightens and her carefully balanced life starts to unravel, Emilia is forced to confront the fears she’s buried beneath ambition and silence: the loneliness, the exhaustion, and the aching desire to be more than a name. The answers she’s searching for won’t be found in equations or blueprints—but in late-night conversations, unfinished confessions, and the steady presence of the one infuriating mechanic who sees her too clearly and refuses to let her disappear behind her legacy.
Because some legacies lift you higher.
And some threaten to break you apart.
In the space between who she’s expected to be and who she’s becoming, Emilia must decide what she’s willing to risk—her dreams, her heart, or the fragile hope of finally being seen.

It was all the things a sky should not be all at once and her reptilian brain was just about screaming in horror at it all and… That really did not make in any less beautiful, did it? A cosmic spectacle out of a space opera writer’s weirdest fever dream. Simply…“Breathtaking,” she says and there’s just a little too much awe in that single word, but… there really is no putting it any other way.“Probably leaking all kinds of exotic radiations all over us, but… You wanted superpowers of your own, right?”She rolls her eyes at that and says nothing, because some of his nonsense there is no dignifying with an answer. “You shouldn’t be anywhere near here,” Spider-Man insisted, posture tightening.
Steve quickly stepped in, “What he meant to say is we’re very sorry we missed you. This was a highly dangerous attack.”
“We know,” came a nonchalant voice from the shop doorway. A young woman had emerged without Wanda’s notice, nor, judging by his quick step away, Spider-Man’s. She wore a collared shirt and a name tag that read MICHELLE, lifting the rolling pin held in her hand. “We had it handled.”
Spider-Man glanced between them, backing away. When he spoke, it wasn’t with the sure compassion he usually held for New Yorkers. His words shook; he was angry. “You could have been seriously hurt! What the hell were you thinking? Are you stupid?”

summary: When falling, there's always this sense of weightlessness, a rush of adrenaline. Panic would overtake you as your stomach drops as gravity pulls you back down to the ground. Peter has grown used to the feeling, the dropping feeling becoming a part of his every day since he was 14 years old. He finds a comfort in the weightlessness, the rush of wind against his ears and brushing through the fabric of his suit. Suddenly, everything that's happened to him is insignificant compared to the flow of air and the calculations of how to swing or fall.He has always heard other people talking about the moment before falling, or how the impact to the ground felt afterwards. They've heard of the wounds, of the deaths, failed landings and miscalculations. He's had his fair share of those, bruises racking his body from building corners unavoided and scrapes from hitting the ground. He's heard stories, even been a part of a few.("Thank you, thank you, thankyouthankyouthankyou." "Oh my god I didn't–") Yet he hasn't heard about others' experiences in the fall. summary: “What’s your name, soldier?” A voice asks him from above, leaning over him and blocking the ceiling lights. Just a dark silhouette among the shadows. Something in the back of Peter’s mind sends shivers down his spine and warnings blare in his head, but he’s too tired to understand.Peter swallows, his mouth dry like sandpaper, thirsty. “Peter.” He responds.The person above him sighs deeply, shaking their head. The sound is so far away, like underwater. “Guess we’re not quite finished with you yet,” The voice tells him, a hand coming down to brush against his forehead. A gentle touch, that Peter can’t keep himself from leaning into there. There’s a flicker of memory before his eyes, of rough hands, carding through his curls and the smell of oil and the sound of an arc reactor. What’s an arc reactor? Peter asks himself silently. Whose hands had been carding through his hair? summary:
Peter’s hand stilled on his fries, and he looked down, studying the paper wrapper on the dingy plastic tray. It occurred to him, then, just how true Happy’s words rang. Tony would show he cared in these grand gestures, in the things he’d build and plan and anticipate, but never in the simple words Peter thought would make it feel real. Growing up, May and Ben were polar opposites— they didn’t have the money or the materials for the grand gestures, but Peter had never doubted he’d been loved, in the simplest profession of words. Tony was… not like that, not in the slightest. It felt as though Peter were trying to read a different language entirely, attempting to parse the deeper meaning without even having a basic grasp on the vocabulary.
OR: Happy Hogan, serving as the in-between for a stubborn eccentric genius friend he's known for decades, and the recently acquired Spider-kid he's taken a begrudging fondness to; forcing them to reconcile their differences and talk to each other about their similarities, rather than stubbornly bottling everything up.(AKA: helping them find a happy medium, if you will.)
